RECOMMENDATION (Para 13)
 
11.       The Committee feels that the issue relating to the safety and security of the tourists, especially foreign tourists is
 very important and needs to be looked into seriously.  The Committee is of the view that incidents of harassment of
 foreign tourists bring a bad name to the country and have an adverse effect on the foreign tourist arrival.  Deployment
 of Special Tourism Police Force can be an effective tool for ensuring safety and security of the tourists.  The
 Committee appreciates the creation of the Special Tourism Police Force by some of the states.  The Committee also
 suggests that the police personnel of the States should also be provided special 'tourist-oriented' training.  Such form of
 official protection to international and domestic tourists would certainly instil confidence amongst the tourists visiting
 these territories.  A successful implementation of such measures will definitely encourage the other State Governments
 in implementing similar schemes for the promotion of tourism in their respective States.
 
Reply of the Government
 
12.       The Governments of Kerala, J&K, Rajasthan, Goa, Himachal Pradesh, Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh have
 set-up Tourist Police Force for the safety and security of the foreign tourists.
 
13.       Government of Delhi, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Chandigarh are in the process of setting
 up of Tourist Police Force.
 
14.       Some of the States/UTs e.g. Mizoram, Daman & Diu, Assam, Sikkim, Pondicherry, Lakshadweep have not felt
 the necessity of the Tourist Police Force and have instructed the regular police force to look into safety and security of
 the foreign tourists.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
 
15.       The Committee notes the reply of the Government.
 
RATIONALISATION OF TAXES ON THE TOURISM INDUSTRY
RECOMMENDATION (Para 19)  
 
16.       The Committee feels that the hotel industry is the backbone of tourism.  The major share of tourism revenue to
 the government is contributed by this sector.  However, there are a lot of taxes and sometimes duplication of taxes at
 both Central and State levels on the hotel sector.  The multiple taxes have imposed a heavy financial burden on the
 hotel industry.  The Committee observes that taxes on hotel rooms and food levied by both the Centre and the States
 add upto over 45 percent, making the industry grossly uncompetitive.  The Committee is of the view that there ought to
 be coordination and synergy between the Centre and the State Governments on the tax front and that there is an urgent
 need to rationalize both Central and State taxes on tourism.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Central
 Government/State Governments must come forward with rationalisation of taxes and provide concessions for the hotel
 industry to give a fillip to the arrival of the tourists in the States.  Further there should be uniformity in the rate of
 various taxes levied by the State Governments on the hotel industry.
 
Reply of the Government
 
17.       The Department of Tourism has been taking steps for the rationalization of taxes levied by the Central
 Government and the State Governments. 
 
18.       Several taxes on the hotel industry like Luxury Tax and Sales Tax are levied by the State Governments.  These
 taxes coupled with the Expenditure Tax levied by the Central Govt. impose a heavy burden on the hotel industry, which
 is passed on to the occupants, thereby increasing the cost of accommodation.
 
19.       In the meeting of Chief Ministers and Tourism Ministers of all States held on 30.10.2001, the State Governments
 were requested to rationalise these taxes.  Again in a meeting held on 5.9.2002 of all the Tourism Ministers and the
 tourism Secretaries, this issue was again taken up with the State Governments.

20.       As regards the levies of the Central Governments, the issue was taken up with the Ministry of Finance in the
 Department of Tourism’s Pre-budget Memorandum for the year 2002-03.  As a result following measures were
 announced in the Budget 2002-03:-
 
Expenditure Tax:
Expenditure Tax on hotels to apply only to room charges henceforth: earlier expenditure tax was charged
 on room charges as well as other services. Threshold of Rs.2000 raised to Rs.3000 for levy of
 expenditure tax.
 
Service Tax:
Service Tax exemption given earlier to be extended for one more year; in  case of functions and banquets
 where the entire bill is for catering services, no service tax would be charged.
 
80HHC and 80 HHD:
Disparities between 80HHC AND 80 HHD removed.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
 
21.       The Committee appreciates the steps taken by the Department of Tourism towards rationalisation of
 taxes levied by the Central Government and State Government.  The Committee also appreciates the measures
 announced by the Government in the Budget 2002-03 though State Governments have not yet taken any decision
 on rationalisation of taxes.  The Committee recommends that Department of Tourism should pursue the State
 Governments for rationalisation of different taxes and provide incentives for the hotel Industry so as to boost
 this Industry at large and to generate tourist arrivals.
 
RATIONALISATION OF TAXES ON THE TOURISM INDUSTRY
RECOMMENDATION (Para 20)
 
22.       The Committee observes that there is a lack of uniformity in taxes, laws and regulation across the States.  While
 the State Governments are taking steps to develop tourism in their respective states, the lack of coordination among
 them and the higher rates of road tax/disparity in the taxes in the states, especially southern States have had negative
 effect on the growth of tourism in these states.  These factors also result in hardships for the tourists as also increase the
 cost of travel for the tourists.  The Committee therefore, recommends that there should be a composite transport permit
 for tourist vehicles.  The Committee also recommends that the Central and the State Governments should take
 immediate steps to create uniformity between the local vehicles and the visiting vehicles.  Steps should also be taken to
 facilitate easy travel and free inter-State movement for tourist vehicles.
 
Reply of the Government
 
23.       As regards the taxes on the travel sector, these taxes are levied by the respective State Governments.  Not only
 are the rates of these levies are very high, but even the mode of levy varies from State to State.
 
24.       The Department of tourism took up this matter with the State Government. in the Tourism Minister’s
 Conference.
 
25.       The matter was also taken up with the Ministry of Highways and Road Transport.  They had included this
 subject as an agenda in the Transport Development Council attended by the Transport Ministers and the Transport
 Secretaries of the State Governments.  Though this matter was discussed a consensus could not be arrived at to resolve
 the issue.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE

26.       The Committee understands the compulsions of the Department of Tourism in enforcing the composite
 transport permit for tourism vehicles.  The Committee, however, recommends that Department of Tourism
 should keep pursuing the State Governments for bringing uniformity in taxes, laws and regulation for reduction
 of road taxes etc. to facilitate easy travel and free inter-state movement of tourist vehicles.    
 
TOURISM DEVELOPMENT IN ANDAMAN & NICOBAR AND LAKSHADWEEP ISLANDS
 
RECOMMENDATION (Para 24)
 
27.       The Committee feels that Andaman & Nicobar and Lakshadweep Islands have the potential of growing into top
 destinations for beach tourism and water sports.  But for the constraint of transportation of tourists from the mainland,
 these islands would have attracted a still larger number of tourists, earning revenue and generating employment for the
 local islanders.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the work on the extension of runway at Port Blair may be
 completed at the earliest and the frequency of flights may also be increased so that more and more tourists are able to
 land there.  The Committee welcomes the decision of DGCA to permit the foreign tourist charter flights to land at Port
 Blair and recommends that this fact may be given wide publicity amongst national as well as international tour
 operators.  Similarly, round the year air services, well connected with other important centres like Kochi,
 Thiruvananthapuram and Goa may be introduced to give a boost to the development and promotion of tourism in the
 Lakshadweep Islands. Further, clearance to the proposals for construction of airfields at Kavarati, Minicoy, Andrott,
 Kadmat and Kiltan Islands should be expedited.  The Committee also feels that creating eco-friendly tourist
 infrastructure and water sports facility involves huge expenditure.  Due to the limited resources available to these two
 Union Territories, it may not be possible for the administration of these islands to create infrastructure and other
 facilities in the islands.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the administration of these islands should create
 conducive atmosphere for private investment and, thereafter, invite private sector participation in developing the
 necessary infrastructure, accommodation and high quality eco-friendly tourists/resorts.
 
Reply of the Government
 
28.       The Administrator of A&N Islands and Lakshadweep Islands/DGCA have been requested to develop
 infrastructure for the promotion of tourism and for creation of conducive atmosphere for private investment and invite
 private sector participation in developing the necessary infrastructure, accommodation and high quality eco-friendly
 tourist resorts but no reply has been received from the above mentioned departments.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
 
29.       The Committee notes the reply and recommends that the Department of Tourism should keep pursuing
 the matter vigorously with the administration of A&N Islands and Lakshadweep Islands.
 
PERMIT SYSTEM FOR THE TOURISTS
RECOMMENDATION (Paras 26 & 28)
 
30.       The Committee is of the view that foreign tourists constitute an important component of tourists who wish to
 visit the Andaman & Nicobar and Lakshadweep Islands.  The restrictions on foreigners to stay beyond permitted period
 in the Islands and visiting only selected islands has discouraged the foreigners from visiting these islands.  The
 Committee, therefore, recommends that in order to optimally exploit the potential of tourism in these islands, the
 restrictions on the foreigners on visiting the islands may be removed and they may be permitted to stay/enjoy the
 beauty of the islands for longer periods.  The Committee also feels that opening up new islands for foreigners also
 needs to be given priority and recommends that the Central Department of Tourism should take up the proposal
 regarding opening up of more islands for the foreign tourists with the Ministry of Home Affairs.
 
31.       The Committee appreciates the Government for having opened some areas of Nagaland for foreign tourists and

 is of the view that the levying of U.S. Dollars 30 from the foreigners who wished to visit Sikkim will discourage the
 foreign tourists from visiting Sikkim.  The Committee recommends that the government should consider abolishing the
 permit system for foreign tourists, as has been done in the case of Assam and Meghalaya.  The Committee hopes that it
 will definitely help in boosting foreign tourist arrivals in the state.
 
Reply of the Government
 
32.       The matter has been taken up with the Ministry of Home Affairs regarding the opening of more islands in A&N
 and Lakshadweep and abolishing of permit system as was being done in Assam and Meghalaya.  The Committee ’s
 views on the effecting of the levy of USD 30 from foreigners visting Sikkim has also been communicated.  A reply
 from the Ministry of Home Affairs is awaited and the Standing Committee will be apprised of action taken by the
 Ministry of Home Affairs as soon as their reply is received.

 that it should be expedited at an early date.
 
CONSTRAINT OF COASTAL REGULATION ZONE ACT
RECOMMENDATION (Para 30)
 
34.       The Committee is of the view that the impact of tourism on the environment and ecology requires serious
 consideration.  There is no doubt that unplanned tourism not only degrades the environment physically and otherwise
 but also carries the seeds of its own destruction.  However, the Committee feels that the provisions of CRZ Act do not
 take into account the unique features of the coastal lines of various States in the country, particularly of Andaman &
 Nicobar and Lakshadweep Islands and Kerala.  India has many beautiful beaches, which can be developed from
 tourism point of view.  The Committee recommends that the Government should, therefore, seriously consider relaxing
 the provisions of the Costal Regulation Zone Act.  The Ministry of Environment and Forests should also take a liberal
 view and consider positively the proposals seeking relaxation of CRZ restrictions for tourism projects.
 
Reply of the Government
 
35.       Department of Tourism, Government of India has taken up the issue with the Ministry of Environment & Forests
 to relax CRZ Regulations as it poses serious impediment in the development of beach tourism and have suggested that
 the Notification may be modified to enable State Governments to undertake tourism activities.  A recommendation has
 also been made that certain specified areas may be treated as Special Tourism economic Zones.
 
36.       In the case of Andaman & Nicobar Islands the Department of Tourism has proposed to constitute a High
 Powered Committee under the Chairmanship of Minister of Tourism & Culture comprising of the following members
 to discuss, finalise and approve all tourism projects relating to Andaman & Nicobar Islands:

      3.    Secretary(Tourism), Government of India
      4.    Secretary, Ministry of Environment and Forests
      5.    Chief Secretary, Andaman & Nicobar Islands
      6.    Joint Secretary, (NAVY), Ministry of Defence
      7.    Joint Secretary (UT), Ministry of Home Affairs
      8.    Joint Secretary, Department of Tourism             --         Convenor

37.       The Committee appreciates the steps taken by the Department of Tourism to constitute a High Powered
 Committee to discuss, finalise and approve all tourism projects relating to A&N Islands and recommends that
 similar action be taken to sort out the problem relating to CRZ regulations.
LACK OF CONNECTIVITY
RECOMMENDATION (Para 32)
 
38.       The Committee feels that there exists a fairly large domestic tourist movement in the country.  However, one
 major stumbling block before the inter-state tourism is poor connectivity.  Domestic Tourism cannot be promoted
 unless the air, rail and road links across the various states and places of tourist interest in the country are improved.  In
 absence of a comfortable access to the places of tourist interest, the tourist cannot be encouraged to visit such places. 
 The Committee, therefore, recommends, that the tourist destinations in the country should be well connected by rail,
 road and air with the urban centres/cities of the region to ensure easy accessibility.  Also the movement of the trains
 should be regularised and speeded up.  The Committee also feels that tourism is closely interlinked with the Civil
 Aviation Sector.  Air linking of the various tourist places in the country as well as places abroad from where tourist
 arrival is expected is essential for development of tourism in the country.  The Committee also recommends that efforts
 should be made to explore the possibility of upgrading the Veer Sarvarkar Airport at Port Blair and Bagdogra Airport
 into international airports so that these places could find a place on the international tourist map.  Also, The Ministries
 of Civil Aviation and Railways should take steps for providing the necessary infrastructure and improve air and rail
 connectivity to the various states in the country.
 
Reply of the Government
 
39.       The matter has been taken up with the Director General Civil Aviation, Ministry of Railway for raising/boosting
 the connectivity in all the tourist destinations.  The Committee has recommended the need of upgrading the Veer
 Sarvarkar Airport at Port Blair and Bagdogra Airport into international airports so that these places could find a place
 on the International Tourists Map and this has also been taken up with the DGCA.  As and when the reply is received
 from the above authorities, the Standing Committee will be apprised of the action taken by the Ministry of Railways/the
 Director General Civil Aviation for increasing tourism connectivity to the tourist destinations as well as upgrading the
 domestic airports to international airports.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
 
40.       The Committee notes the reply and recommends the Department of Tourism to vigorously pursue the
 matter with the Ministry of Railways and the Director General Civil Aviation for increasing tourism
 connectivity to the tourist destinations as well as upgrading of domestic airports to international airports.

INTRODUCTION
         I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism & Culture,
 having been authorised by the Committee to present on its behalf, do hereby present this Seventy-third Report of the
 Committee on the Action Taken by the Government on the recommendations/observations contained in its Sixty-sixth
 Report on Demands for Grants (2003-2004) of Department of Tourism.
2.      The Sixty-sixth Report of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism and
 Culture was presented to both the Houses of Parliament on 10
th April 2003.
 
3.      Action Taken Replies on the recommendations of the Committee contained in its Sixty-sixth Report were received
 from the Department of Tourism on 17th July 2003.
 
4.      The Committee considered the subject and adopted the Report in its meeting held on 29th October 2003.
 
NEW DELHI
October 29, 2003
Kartika 7, 1925 (Saka)                                   
NILOTPAL BASU
 Chairman,
Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee
 on Transport, Tourism & Culture.
REPORT
           
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Government on the observations/recommendations as
 contained in its Sixty-sixth Report on Demands for Grants (2003-04) (Demand No. 91) of the Department of Tourism which
 was presented to the Parliament on 10th April 2003.
 
2.         Action Taken Replies have been received from the Government on 17 th July 2003 in respect of all the
 observations/recommendations contained in the Report.  These have been categorized as follows:-
 
(i)                  Recommendations/observations that have been accepted by the Government:
 
Para Nos. 15, 20, 24 & 29                                                                     Total - 4
 
(ii)                Recommendations/observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue in view of the Government replies:
 
Para Nos. 34 & 45                                                                                Total – 2
 
(iii)               Recommendations/observations in respect of which replies of the Government have not been accepted by the
 Committee.
 
      Nil                                                                                                   Total - 0
 
(iv)              Recommendations/observations in respect of which final replies of the Government are still awaited:
 
Para Nos. 7, 9, 26, 40, 50, 51, 55, 56 & 59                                               Total - 9
 
3.         The Committee desires that final replies in respect of the recommendations, which have been categorized as
 interim replies by the Committee should be furnished to it at the earliest.
 
4.         On scrutiny of the said Action Taken Replies, the Committee has made observations on each item of the action
 taken/proposed to be taken by the Ministry.  The recommendations of the Committee contained in the Sixty-sixth Report, action
 taken thereon by the Government and recommendations/observations of the Committee on each item of action taken have been
 given in the succeeding paragraphs.
 
THE APPROACH IN THE 10 TH PLAN AND ANALYSIS OF THE ANNUAL PLAN 2003-04 (Recommendation at

 paras 7 and 9)
 
5.         The Committee is happy to note that the plan allocation of Rs.225.00 crores of the Department of Tourism was not
 subjected to any reduction at R.E. stage during 2002-2003 and the outlay for the year 2003-2004 has also been hiked
 substantially from Rs.225.00 crores to Rs.325.00 crores.  The Committee hopes that the maximum amount of plan outlay would
 be utilised properly and substantially during the first five months of the current financial year so that the Department will be in
 a position to make demand for more allocation of funds at R.E. stage   for development of tourism infrastructure and promotion
 of tourism in the country.
 
6.         The Committee notes that for the financial year 2002-03, the expenditure upto January 2003 has been only 55% i.e.
 Rs.124.876 crores out of the total plan allocation of Rs.225 crores.  Though, the Department of Tourism have assured that the
 total allocation would be spent by the end of the financial year i.e. 31st March 2003 the Committee however, is unable to
 understand as to how the Department would be able to spend the remaining 45% of the plan allocation within a short span of
 just 2 months of the financial year.  The Committee therefore, disapproves the tendency of spending funds desperately towards
 the end of the financial year. The Committee recommends that the Department should evolve some mechanism of uniform
 utilization pattern through out the year so as to avoid incurring expenditure at the fag end of the financial year.
 
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
 
7.         The Department of Tourism has formulated schemes of Integrated Development of Tourist Circuits,
 Product/Infrastructure and Destination Development and Assistance for Large Revenue Generating Products during the year
 2002-03, the first year of the Tenth Five Year Plan. Schemes were formulated in consultation with the Planning Commission. 
 Being restructured schemes SFC meetings were called for approval and release of funds.  It took time in finalisation of these
 schemes.  State Governments/UT Administrations were requested to submit detailed projects proposals for these schemes.  As
 the State Governments submitted the proposals after preparing detailed project reports, there was delay in release of funds to
 the State Governments.  But the Department of Tourism utilized the allocated funds of Rs.225 crores during the year 2002-03. 
 In fact the Department of Tourism sought additional grants of Rs.34.50 crores for completion of old projects.  Additional funds
 of Rs.25.00 crores were provided in March 2003 and these were fully utilized.  The recommendation of the Committee will be
 followed by the Department and efforts will be made for uniform utilization of funds during the year 2003-04. 
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
 
8.         The Committee notes that the Department of Tourism has formulated schemes of Integrated Development of
 Tourist Circuits, Product/Infrastructure and Destination Development and Assistance for Large Revenue Generating
 Products during the year 2002-03.  However, the Committee desires that State Governments may be given some
 reasonable time and  requested to submit project proposals for the schemes within that stipulated time limit only for
 avoiding delays in finalisation of project proposals.  The Committee also recommends that old pending projects must
 also be completed by the Department of Tourism and if need be, additional grants may also be provided.
 
INTEGRATED DEVELOPMENT OF TOURIST CIRCUITS
(Recommendation at para 15)
 
9.         The Committee is happy to note that Department of Tourism is taking a holistic approach for development of these six
 tourist circuits in the country on each year and providing necessary infrastructural facilities within these circuits and
 convergence of resources in coordination with States/Private sector.  The Committee also notes that Department of Tourism has
 decided that in future funds will not be provided to small isolated projects, which are not of much importance for the
 development of tourism in the country and concentrate on the development of important travel circuits alone.  The Committee
 recommends that more tourist circuits region wise covering more than a State/UT may be selected and developed on the basis
 of the tourism potential of the places according to international standards and aggressive marketing efforts may be taken up in
 order to attract more and more tourists to these places. 
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT

RURAL TOURISM
(Recommendation at para 24)
 
17.        The Rural Tourism is a new market concept to tap tourist traffic as it can form the perfect vehicle for achievement of the
 national objective of achieving partnerships between local communities, government and industry.  Besides, it would help
 generate employment at local level, dispensing with the need of migrations to distant places for earning livelihood thereby
 leading to economic betterment. The Rural Tourism can also provide a solution to the increasing trends of industrialization and
 help in countering the stress of urban life styles and other urbanization syndromes. The Committee feels that global tourism
 growth potential can be harnessed as a strategy for Rural Development and therefore, recommends that the Department of
 Tourism should develop a strong platform around the concept of Rural Tourism for achieving the national objectives in better
 perspective.

04.  Planning Commission has agreed for a provision of 15 crores exclusively for Rural Tourism Projects.

20.        The Committee notes that the efforts being made by the Department of Tourism for development of rural
 tourism in the country during the year 2003-04.  The Committee is of the view that the funds which are being
 earmarked exclusively for Rural Tourism Projects should be utilized properly in order to tap tourist traffic globally.

 cruise vessels. The Committee however, couldn’t understand as to how the scheme has been finalized when the proposals under
 the scheme are yet to be received by the department of tourism. It shows that the Department is lacking pro-active approach in

REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
 
22.        The Department of Tourism formulated the scheme ‘Assistance for Large Revenue Generating Projects’ during the year
 2002-03, the first year of the Tenth Five Year Plan in consultation with the Planning Commission A budget provision of
 Rs.6.00 crore was earmarked for this scheme during 2002-03.  The objective of the scheme is to strengthen tourist infrastructure
 in the country through Public and Private Sector partnership.  During the year 2002-03 the entire budget provision of Rs.6.00
 crores has been spent for the projects under this scheme.
 
23.        The recommendation of the Committee will be followed and the State Governments/UT Administrations have already
 been requested vide Letter dated 24
th April 2003 to submit the project proposals for consideration during the year 2003-04.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
 
24.        The Committee notes that the Department of Tourism have requested the State Governments/UT Administration
 for submission of project under large revenue generating projects scheme to strengthen tourist infrastructure through
 public and private sector partnership in their respective states and recommends that Department of Tourism should
 keep pursuing the State Governments/UT Administration for timely submission of projects under the scheme.
 
CAPACITY BUILDING FOR SERVICE PROVIDERS
(Recommendation at para 29)
 
25.        The Committee appreciates the scheme launched by the Department of Tourism for training the persons in an
 unorganized sector consisting of small hotel, dhabas and restaurant and other eatable joints spread all over the country
 including tourists guides. The Committee is of the opinion since tourism industry plays a nodal role in displaying the rich
 cultural heritage to the world at large, and possesses high employment potential, personnel engaged in this sector are different
 from those required by personnel engaged in other sectors.  The Committee hopes that this would adequately cater to the
 training needs of the persons engaged in the unorganized sector and helps them is upgrading their quality.  The Committee
 desires that sufficient funds should be allocated under this head and efforts should be made to make the scheme more effective
 by expanding its coverage to the important tourist circuits/tourist destinations.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
 
26.        The Department of Tourism has formulated the “Guidelines” for the newly launched scheme of “Capacity Building for
 Service Providers” to standardize and also to make the scheme effective.  Under the scheme, training will be provided by
 Institutes of Hotel Management/Food Craft Institutes/Indiatourism Offices and Indian Institute of Tourism & Travel
 Management to the service providers in the unorganized sector.  In order to provide uniformity in the training Department of
 Tourism is formulating model/standard “Training Programme Modules” as well as an “Annual Calendar of Training
 Programmes” for the implementing institutions.
 
27.        During the year 2002-03 the Budget allocation of Rs.150 lakhs under the scheme was fully utilized by providing funds
 to IHMs and Food Craft Institutes.  In the current financial year i.e. 2003-04 there is a provision of Rs.200 lakhs allocated under
 this Head and funds shall be released to Indiatourism Offices and IITTM also, in addition to the IHMs and FCIs.  The
 Department shall follow a monitoring mechanism to review and monitor the training programmes conducted by various
 institutions to make the scheme more effective and uniformly implemented so as to cover the important tourist destinations in
 the country.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE

 training programmes conducted by various institutions to make the scheme more effective and uniformly implemented
 so as to cover the important tourist destinations in the country.  The Committee further recommends that monitoring
 mechanism should be adequately strengthened to ensure quality training.
 
OVERSEAS PROMOTION AND MARKETING
(Recommendation at para 34)
 
29.        The Committee observes that though the allocation for overseas promotion and publicity has been increased
 substantially during the year 2003-04 still there is a significant gap between the Government of India’s spending and the world
 average expenditure on travel and tourism which can not be abridged keeping in view the crunch of financial resources. The
 Committee also notes that Department of Tourism has reoriented itself to the overseas market with a view to changing global
 scenario and fierce competition in the tourism generating markets. The Committee however, recommends that Department of
 Tourism should consider new strategy in the changing patterns of consumer behaviour and adopts integrated marketing
 communication approach to secure the future of the industry and its potentiality for job creations. 
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
 
30.        The Department of Tourism has noted the above recommendation and also taken into account the present world travel
 trends and changing patterns of consumer behavior while developing its Promotional Plan for the current financial year.  The
 Plan adopts an integrated marketing communications approach and the elements include advertising, sales promotion, public
 relations and direct marketing for positioning India in key markets under the brand name ‘Incredible India’.
 
31.        In the changing world tourism scenario where mass markets are getting fragmented and destinations are shifting away
 from mass marketing to segmented marketing, the Department lays emphasis on use of information technology and Internet as
 this medium has become a catalyst in this paradigm shift.
 
32.        The plan also envisages a centralized advertising campaign to be launched directly from the Headquarters  in various
 key markets.  The Indiatourism Offices overseas through their annual Action Plans would supplement this campaign as well as
 compliment with promotional activities like participation in fairs and exhibitions, organising of seminars and workshops, direct
 mailing, hosting of media personalities and opinion makers under the Hospitality programme, web marketing, dissemination of
 information through the CD-ROMs and brochures etc.  The main objective behind this strategy is to carefully integrate and
 coordinate various communication channels so as to deliver a clear, consistent and compelling message about India’s various
 tourism products under the brand line ‘Incredible India’.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
 
33.        The Committee notes that the Department of Tourism has developed the promotional plan keeping in view the
 changing global scenario and competition in the tourism generating markets.  The Committee appreciates the
 Department of Tourism for adopting an integrated marketing communications approach, components of which include
 advertising, sales promotion, public relations and direct marketing for positioning India in key markets under the
 brand name ‘Incredible India’ as per its recommendation.  The Committee wishes that it will help augmenting the
 tourism potential and in view of this desires not to pursue the matter further.
 
TOURISM AND ITS IMPACT ON INDIA’S GROSS DOMESTIC PRODUCT
 (Recommendation at para 40)
 
34.        The Committee is of the opinion that domestic tourism has to act as a pillar of our future tourism policy besides as a
 major engine for economic growth of the country and there is a need to provide strong support to this sector in the form of large
 infrastructure.  The Committee is not satisfied with the efforts of the Department of Tourism due to which India’s share of

 newly constituted bodies like National Tourism Advisory Council, Inter-ministerial coordination group etc. should hold
 meetings regularly and Department of Tourism should bring all contentious issues before these bodies in a proactive
 manner.

 coordination with each other for the development of tourists sector in the country as per the recommendation of the

 peak travel months ranging from October to March and especially from major tourism originating destination like North
 America, Western Europe and South East Asia.   The additional seat capacity from the major destinations would provide
 impetus to tourism and have a positive impact on economic development of India.

40.        The Committee is of the opinion that the potential of domestic tourism has grown substantially during the last few years

 be developed soon. For this purpose possibility of getting foreign assistance and Private Sector participation should also be

 public convenience facilities at the important tourist destinations.  This may be done with the involvement of State
 Government/Local bodies/Municipal Corporation. The Committee notes the reply of the Department of Tourism on the
 recommendation of the Committee contained at Para 60 of the 55
th report which says that: -
 
"The recommendation of the Standing Committee and the provision of luggage carrying trolleys at the station,
 which are of tourism importance has been noted by the Ministry of Railways, Railway Board."
 
41.        The Committee is not satisfied with the lackadaisical attitude of the Department of Tourism in taking up the matter with
 Ministry of Railways.   The Committee should be informed about the actual action taken by the Ministry of Railways in this
 regard and in this connection Committee reiterates its earlier recommendation contained in 55th Report, which is reproduced
 below;
 
 “The committee recommends that the Department of Tourism should take up with the Ministry of Railways for

 kind that are available at the airports. These trolleys could be made available to the tourists against payment as in

43.        The Ministry of Railways is running regular Rajdhani, Shatabdi and Janshatabdi Express trains connecting various
 tourists places.  The Railways, however, has welcomed the proposal of running special tourist trains with private sector
 participation subject to operational and financial viability.
 
44.        The Ministry of Railways have noted the recommendation of the Standing Committee regarding the provision of
 alternative methods of carrying baggage at the Railway Stations like trolleys etc. and information of action taken in this regard
 is being collected.

 with private sector for the tourists at different locations in India and a proposal for running special tourist trains with
 private sector participation is under consideration of Ministry of Railways.  However, Committee desires that

(c)        Coordination Between Department of Tourism and State Governments
(Recommendation at paras 55 and 56)          
           
46.        The Committee notes with dismay that during the 9th Five Year Plan, the Department of Tourism sanctioned 1563
 projects involving an amount of Rs.372.43 crores to the State Government/UTs for tourism projects out of which only 571
 projects have been completed and 992 projects remained incomplete. Non-completion of projects not only led to cost over runs
 of the project but also the tourists potential in the country could not be exploited fully in the absence of the facilities which
 could have been made available otherwise.  The Committee is unable to understand the reason put forth by the Department of
 Tourism for delay i.e. lack of coordination between the State Government and different other Ministries in the implementation
 of projects, besides low level of monitoring and review of progress.  The Committee is of the opinion that involvement of
 Members of Parliament in identification, development and monitoring of tourist destinations in their respective state, can avoid
 delay and cost overrun in execution of tourism projects. In this connection, the committee reiterates its earlier recommendation
 made in 55th Report, which is reproduced below;
 
“The Committee recommends that the Department of Tourism should involve the Members of Parliament in the
 identification and development of places of tourist interest in their respective states.  The Committee is of the view that,
 as elected representatives of the people, Members of Parliament can also help the Department in identifying tourism
 sports in their states and inform the Department of Tourism which can take steps to develop such tourism areas.  The
 Committee also recommends that the Department of Tourism should, by way of taking the initiative, request the
 Members of Parliament to identify places, which can be developed as tourist spots.  The Members of Parliament should
 also be kept informed of the status of the tourism projects in their respective states.”
 
47.        The Committee therefore recommends that Department of Tourism should directly involve the Member of Parliament in
 identification, development and monitoring process of tourists destinations/circuits in their respective states and have a task
 force which will coordinate between different Ministries as well as State Governments and respective Members of Parliament
 in that state for monitoring the progress of physical targets every quarter or so.

4.         The Committee appreciates that except for a few slippages, the Golden Quadrilateral programme is largely on
 track and is likely to be substantially completed by the targeted period i.e. December 2003. The Committee also expects
 that the projects funded by the World Bank would also be completed by the recommended targeted period, i.e. March
 2005.  However, the Committee is not happy to note that every year the Ministry is furnishing same reasons such as land
 acquisition, removal of utilities, environmental/forest clearances, quarries etc. for delay in the execution of the
 projects.   The Government should be careful in handling court cases because if the cases are not handled properly, it
 would lead to further undue delay. The Committee, therefore, recommends that Ministry of Road Transport &
 Highways should evolve some mechanism to identify the traditional bottlenecks, which are causing delay and involve
 all the concerned agencies in the process of resolving all such hindrances.

 people living along the length of the roads. Roads are the key to the development of an economy. The Committee hopes
 that the revolution in the road sector will go a long way in promoting the economic development of the country and
 integrating remote regions with the mainstream economic activity by opening them to trade and investment.

6.         The projects are reviewed at several levels including the Hon’ble Minister of Road Transport & Highways on
 regular bimonthly basis in meetings held with NHAI officials, contractors and supervision consultants.  All matters
 pertaining to land acquisition, removal of utilities, environmental/forest clearances, quarries are taken up with the state
 authorities at the highest level where required.  The Hon’ble Minister has also taken up these issues with the respective
 Chief Ministers of the States.

CENTRAL ROAD FUND (CRF)
(Recommendation at Para 30 and 32)
 
8.         The Committee in its 59
th Report on Demands for Grants 2002-03 of the Ministry of Road Transport and
 Highways had commented upon the savings under Central Road Fund during 2001-02 and recommended that proper
 monitoring for utilisation of funds be ensured.  The Committee appreciates that there has been a major improvement in
 the rate of utilisation of Central Road Fund by the States/UTs as compared to the earlier years.  The Committee notes
 with satisfaction that the funds allocated for maintenance and development of National Highways to the States/UTs was
 expected to be fully utilised by them during 2002-03.  The Committee recommends that there should be no let up in the
 measures adopted for the complete utilisation of the funds by the States/UTs and the said trend should continue in the
 future also.
 
9.         The Committee is of the view that since the allocation out of the CRF for the State Highways is done by the
 Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, it becomes the responsibility of the Ministry to ensure proper utilisation of
 the funds.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways should develop
 some mechanism to ensure that the funds released out of the CRF for State Highways are utilised for that purpose only.

10.       The States/UTs are required to furnish the progress report and Utilization Certificate in the format prescribed
 vide the Ministry’s guidelines dated 13th July, 2001.  Furnishing of Utilization  Certificate authenticated by an officer of
 the rank of Under Secretary or above of the State/UT and progress report giving the physical and financial progress of
 the CRF works as per the Ministry’s guidelines mentioned above is mandatory for consideration of further release of

11.       The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.
 
MAINTENANCE AND REPAIRS OF NATIONAL HIGHWAYS
(Recommendation at Para 37)
           
12.       The Committee is of the view that if the roads are not well maintained, it would certainly have an adverse impact
 on the aspect of road safety and also the investments made in the construction of the roads go waste.  The Committee is
 constrained to note that the financial resources made available to the Ministry under Maintenance & Repairs head (Non-
Plan) have been only 40% of the requirement projected by the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways.  The Committee
 understands that there is available capacity in the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways to undertake more works for
 maintenance and repair of roads.  The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways should
 utilise funds available for the purpose in the initial few months of the financial year so that the Ministry can
 emphatically impress upon the Government for higher allocation of funds for maintenance and repair of roads at the RE
 stage.  The Committee also recommends that higher allocations be made in the coming years to Ministry of Road
 Transport & Highways for maintenance and repair of roads.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
 
13.       The Ministry is taking necessary steps for sanction of the estimates for maintenance of National Highways
 (Periodic Renewal/Special Repair) in the beginning of the financial year so that the allocated fund can be utilized early
 and additional funds for maintenance can be sought for at the “Revised Estimate” stage.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
 
14.       The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.  The Committee would like to
 be informed of the sanctions made for maintenance of National Highways (Periodical Renewal/Special Repair) by the
 Ministry of Road Transport and Highways upto September 2003 and additional funds sought by the Ministry at the RE
 stage.
 
FEE/TOLL TAX ON BRIDGES AND NATIONAL HIGHWAYS
(Recommendation at Para 42)
 
15.       The Committee is not convinced with the reasons advanced by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways for
 collecting toll on roads and bridges in perpetuity.  The Committee feels that the Government is not justified in
 burdening the common people with the development as well as the maintenance of the roads in the country.  The
 Committee had also commented upon this matter in its 43
rd Report on Demands for Grants 2000-2001 of the then
 Ministry of Surface Transport.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that once the cost of construction of a
 road/bridge plus interest is recovered, the collection of toll should be stopped.   The Committee also feels that there
 exists a need for the rationalisation of the toll tax being charged on the National Highways.  The Committee
 recommends that persons travelling on smaller stretches of the National Highways where toll is being collected should
 be charged a lower amount than the persons using the entire length of that National Highway.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
 
16.       The policy of levying users fee on roads and bridges was adopted to defray the cost of construction and
 maintenance due to budgetary resource constraints.  Levying of users fee is based on the principle of upgradation of the
 facility resulting in reduced vehicle cost, reduced travel time and enhanced safety.  Development and maintenance of
 highways being a continuous process it was decided to levy fee in perpetuity to have constant flow of fund.  The total
 amount of bridge fee as collected is spent in the State from which it is levied.  Thus, this fee is utilized for improving the
 National Highways in the State itself.  In view of the above the Committee may kindly reconsider their

 recommendations.
 
17.       The Users’ fee on National Highways is being collected on “Open Tolling” system.  It means the tolled portion is
 not access controlled.  The users’ fee is charged on the basis of the distance between two tollgates.  The location of
 tollgates is decided on the basis of convenience of traffic, location of major access roads, travel pattern and cost of toll
 collection.  In the ‘Open Tolling’ system it is difficult to implement differential rates of users’ fees.  The users’ fee on
 the basis of distance traveled can be charged in the “Closed Tolling” system where the accesses are controlled.  This is
 not yet feasible in the country.  In view of the above the Committee may kindly reconsider their recommendation.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
 
18.       The Committee does not agree with the reply of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways for collecting toll
 on roads and bridges in perpetuity.  Development and maintenance of highways is no doubt a continuous process but the
 Government cannot absolve itself of its responsibilities in this respect by shifting its entire burden on the common
 people.  In order to help the Government overcome the budgetary financial constraints, the toll should be collected till
 such time the cost of construction of a road/bridge plus interest is recovered.  The Committee, therefore, reiterates its
 earlier recommendation that once the cost of construction of a road/bridge plus interest is recovered, the collection of
 toll should be stopped.
 
19.       The Committee  takes note of the reply of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways with respect to the
 Committee’s recommendation regarding charging of users fee on the basis of distance travelled.  The Committee feels
 that in the present system of tolling, persons traveling in smaller stretches of the National Highways where toll is being
 collected are in a disadvantageous position.  Such a situation cannot be allowed to go on forever.  The Committee,
 therefore, recommends that the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways should initiate the steps to develop a system
 whereby the users’ fee could be charged on the basis of the distance travelled.
 
PORT CONNECTIVITY PROJECTS
(Recommendation at Para 46)
 
20.       The Committee feels that connectivity of the ports to the National Highways is of great importance from the
 point of view of commercial and industrial production.  The Committee is surprised to note that Mumbai Port Trust has
 not been included in the port connectivity projects.  The Committee has been informed that there is no proper road link
 to Mumbai Port and the only available road route to the port is in a poor condition.  The Committee, therefore,
 recommends that the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways should also include the Mumbai Port in their port
 connectivity project.   For this purpose, they can also approach the Mumbai Port Trust for their assistance in the project.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
 
21.       Major ports are to be connected under Port Connectivity Programme as mandated to NHAI.  Feasibility for
 connection of Mumbai Port was examined and it was observed that there was hardly any scope for the improvement of
 approach road to the Mumbai Port as it passed through heavily populated area of Mumbai city.  The only option was to
 construct a new elevated road which would have to pass through long stretch of salt pans and marshy land.  Mumbai
 Port Trust also advised that unless the matters were sorted out, further detailed study should not be carried out.  In view
 of the fact that construction of such a long section of elevated road will be extremely costly and such a huge investment
 might not justify the benefit which will accrue and this would also involve a large extent of land acquisition and
 environmental issued, it was decided not to take up this stretch at this stage.  However, on the advise of the Standing
 Committee the matter is being taken up once again with the Mumbai Port Trust.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE

23.       The Committee is of the view that Members of the Committee, as representatives of the people, can assist and
 coordinate with the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways in the implementation of the projects in their respective
 states.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Members of the Committee should be informed, every three
 months, about the status of the ongoing schemes/projects in all states/UTs as well as about the hindrances faced in the
 implementation of the projects.  It will help the Members of Parliament in taking up and sorting out matters with various
 agencies of the State Government and evolving solutions to the problems faced by the Ministry in achieving their
 objectives.  This will also ensure the smooth and speedy implementation of the projects.  Also it will help the Ministry
 of Road Transport and Highways in doing away with some of the reasons mentioned in para 19 of the Report for delay
 in the execution of the projects which the Ministry is facing every year.

24.       As desired the above mentioned Quarterly Report containing the details of status of on-going Schemes/Projects
 in all States/UTs as well as hindrances faced in the implementation of the projects in respect of NH and other Central
 Sector Road Works will be forwarded regularly directly to the Members of the Standing Committee.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
 
25.       The Committee appreciates that the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways would submit a quarterly Report
 containing the details of status of on-going Schemes/Projects in all States/UTs as well as hindrances faced in the
 implementation of the projects in respect of National Highways and other Central Sector Road Works to the
 Committee.  The Committee is firmly of the view that it will help the Members of Parliament in taking up and sorting
 out matters with various agencies of the State Governments and evolving solutions to the problems which cause delay in
 the execution of road projects.   However, the Committee has been informed that the reports for the quarters ending
 June, September and December 2003 are yet to be furnished.  The Committee desires that the reports should be
 forwarded to the Secretariat at the earliest.
 
ROAD TRANSPORT
(Recommendation at Para 56)
 
26.       The Committee is of the view that road safety is an area of serious concern and the sheer magnitude and severity
 of road accidents in the country requires immediate attention.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the study on
 National Road Safety Policy should be completed at the earliest.  The government should also take measures involving
 technology, education and also enforcement of legal provisions in order to bring down the number of accidents within a
 fixed time frame. 
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
 
27.       The study on National Road Safety Policy is scheduled to be completed within current financial year. The Govt.
 has been taking a number of measures to reduce accidents. Steps taken to prevent accidents broadly fall in three
 categories, namely, Engineering, Education and Enforcement. Government of India has been undertaking a number of
 engineering and educational measures to prevent road accidents in the country. Some of the important steps being taken
 by the Government besides highway design to check the road accidents are as under:

(1)   Assistance for setting up of Driving Training Schools.
(2)   Provision of refresher training to drivers of heavy motor vehicles
(3)      Publicity campaign on Road Safety Awareness through audio-visual-print media.
(4)           Grants-in-aid to voluntary organizations for administrative road safety programmes
(5)    Encouraging use of stimulators in drivers training
(6)           Institution of National Award for voluntary organizations/Individuals for outstanding work in the field of
 Road Safety.
(7)           Organising All India Essay Competition on Road Safety for school children  with a view to create
 awareness
(8)         Tightening of fitness norms for transport vehicles
(9)         Widening/improvement of roads etc.
 
28.            Enforcement of provisions of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 for improved
 road safety is entirely the responsibility of State Government.
 
29.            Upgradation of technology and concomitant norms for safety related automotive components is a continuous
 ongoing exercise.  The automotive standards/norms are gradually being harmonized with ECE specifications.  These
 norms are being constantly upgraded and notified on the basis of recommendations of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules
 Technical Standing Committee.
 
30.       As a result of efforts made by Central/State Governments, accident rate per 1000 vehicles has come down from
 10.98 in 1996 to 8.09 (provisional) in 2000. 
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
 
31.       The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.  The Committee further notes
 that accident rate per 1000 vehicles has come down from 10.98 in 1996 to 8.09 in 2000 and hopes that that steps taken
 by Ministry of Road Transport and Highways would result in further decrease in the accident rate of vehicles which is
 still very high.
 
ROAD TRANSPORT
(Recommendation at Para 58)
 
32.       The Committee feels that with the development and improvement in riding quality of the roads, danger to the
 lives of the villagers and cattle has also increased on those roads.  Inspite of the construction of underpasses at the
 traditional crossing points, the incidents of accidents on such roads has been rising.  The Committee, therefore,
 recommends that while undertaking the development of the roads, the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways should
 make some extra efforts and, if necessary, construct underpasses and over-bridges, taking into account the population
 and the requirement of the users of that area so that accidents can be avoided and there is no loss of lives.  Systematic
 survey for assessment of users convenience should also be conducted in this regard.  
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
 
33.       The four/six laning of National Highway Project considers the provision of under passes and over bridges at
 congested and populated areas for the safety of the habitants in the adjoining areas.  The four/six laning project is
 prepared on the basis of detailed engineering.  The requirement of under passes/over bridges is assessed on the basis of
 number of population and vehicles.  Location of these structures is decided on the basis of engineering requirements and
 also the most preferred point(s) of crossing.  These factors are considered while preparation of the detailed project report
 of the improvement works.  Hence it would be seen that the recommendation of the Hon’ble Standing Committee is
 being followed.

34.       The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.
 
PROBLEM OF OVERLOADING
(Recommendation at Para 65)
 
35.       The Committee is of the view that the problem of overloading of vehicles has been growing steadily inspite of
 the measures adopted by the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways.  The Committee feels that overloading of
 vehicles has not only been causing early destruction of several road stretches but also resulting in accidents leading to
 loss of life and property.  The Committee is constrained to note that certain state governments have been regularising
 overloading for financial gains.  The Committee appreciates the States of Karnataka, West Bengal, Meghalaya, Uttar
 Pradesh, Tripura and Gujarat for offering tax rebate to popularise the use of multi axle vehicles.  The Committee
 recommends that the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways should further take up the matter with the concerned state
 governments so as to check the problem of overloading. Also the legislation proposed for this purpose should be
 introduced at the earliest.  The Committee also reiterates the recommendations made in its 59
th Report that the Ministry
 of Road Transport & Highways should come up with publicity efforts, on large scale, addressing to the truck drivers and
 the agencies engaged in transportation business, including general public.  Themes dealing with dangers of overloading
 should form an important part of the publicity campaigns undertaken in this regard.  Also awareness campaigns should
 be launched including advertisements in print/electronic media. 
 
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
 
36.       Motor Vehicles Act has strict provisions for tackling overloading.  Enforcement of these provisions is
 responsibility of the State Government. The Transport Development Council in its 30th meeting on 16.1.2003 had
 discussed this matter and it was agreed that:
 
a)      Strict enforcement of the provisions relating to overloading under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and Central
 Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989.
b)      The State Governments are not to issue special cards/passes which legalize overloading.
c)      The decision of the 28th meeting of TDC held on 10.10.1998 for states to give a 25% tax rebate to popularize
 use of multi axle vehicles, which has been implemented so far by a few States like Karnataka, West Bengal,
 Meghalaya, Uttar Pradesh, Tripura and Gujarat, may be carried out by other States also.
d)         Keeping in view a number of court cases, the registering authority shall ensure that the vehicles are registered
 only as per the load ceilings notified and in case erroneously a higher load rating has been incorporated, then
 the same shall be got rectified.
e)      Non-renewal of registration and denial of permit to habitual offenders of overloading.
 
Subsequently, this matter has been continuously taken up with the State Governments.
 
37.            MOS(RT&H) and Secretary(RT&H) have written a number of letters to the State Governments pointing out
 that the practice of issuing special cards/ token, which have the effect of legitimizing overloading should be stopped and
 that the Central Government would be constrained to stop the releases from the Central Road Fund to the State
 Governments.   MOS(RT&H) has written to Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh on 3rd April, 2003 and subsequently to
 Chief Ministers of Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Orissa and Haryana on 19.4.2003.  Similarly,
 Secretary(RT&H) has written to all states on 4th March, 2003.  Subsequently, Secretary(RT&H) has again addressed the
 Chief Secretaries of several states, namely Madhya Pradesh & Rajasthan(21.3.2003), Uttar Pradesh, Orissa & Gujarat
 (7.4.2003) and again to Rajasthan, Orissa & Uttar Pradesh (17.4.2003) and Haryana and Uttar Pradesh (on 20.4.2003
 and 29.4.2003 respectively).
 
38.       The Committee’s suggestion regarding making appropriate amendments in the Motor Vehicles Act to tackle
 overloading in an effective manner has been noted.    In fact, a proposal recommending amendment of sec. 194 & 200 of
 the M.V. Act removing the powers of State Governments to compound the offence of overloading has been sent to M/o
 Law for vetting as a part of the comprehensive proposal for amendment of M.V. Act.

39.       As advised by the Committee, the Ministry has taken up in a big way awareness efforts through audio, visual and
 print media about various aspects of road safety which also include the menace of overloading.   These messages are
 addressed to both truck drivers and general public.   The Budget for carrying out various road safety related activities
 has been increased from Rs.25 crores during 2002-2003 to about Rs.35 crores during 2003-2004.

40.       The Committee takes note that the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has been consistently taking up the
 issue of stopping the practice of legalising  overloading of vehicles.  The Committee also notes that the work on the
 proposal recommending amendment of sec. 194 & 200 of the M.V. Act removing the powers of State Governments to
 compound the offence of overloading is under progress.  The Committee recommends that the Government should come
 up with a legislation to this effect after having obtained an explicit consent from the State Governments.
 
COMPUTERISATION OF ROAD TRANSPORT SECTOR
(Recommendation at Para 70)
 
41.       The Committee appreciates the steps taken by the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways in respect of
 computerization of Road Transport Sector.  However, the success achieved in the computerization programme leaves
 much to the desired.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways should
 impress upon the States/UTs for expediting both front-end and back-end computerization programme of the road
 transport sectors.  The Ministry should also explore the possibility of providing financial assistance/incentives to the
 States for completing the computerization programme at the earliest.  This would not only help in putting a curb on the
 tampering of licenses by unscrupulous elements but would also ensure the existence of uniform and foolproof system
 for driving licenses by the various states. 
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
 
42.       The matter has been pursued with the State Governments. It has been learnt that the Ministry of Information
 Technology has launched a scheme to assist development of at least one pilot site in every State. The Ministry has made
 available free of cost, the standardized software for the front end and back end operation of the smart card based Driving
 License and Registration Certificate.  There is no scheme under this Ministry to provide further financial assistance to
 the States/UTs under the Scheme.  However, it has been observed that wherever computerization of RTOs has been
 taken up, revenue gain has been to the tune of 20-40%.  Secretary(RT&H) has written to various Chief Secretaries of the
 States/UTs to provide finance for these programmes as this would pay back the cost quite quickly.  Government agrees
 with the observation of the committee that implementation of the computerization programme by states would help in
 bringing about a uniform & foolproof system for driving licenses.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
 
43.       The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.
 
PERFORMANCE BUDGET
(Recommendation at Para 71)
 
44.       A perusal of the Performance Budget 2003-04 of the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways indicates that the
 Performance Budget lacks the information regarding targets/achievements about the specific schemes undertaken by the
 Ministry during the previous year.  In the absence of the above details, the Committee finds it difficult to assess the
 progress of the projects.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Performance Budget should comprise of
 information indicating the targets fixed with specific parameters, actual physical achievements and slippages alongwith
 the reasons for the same.  The physical/financial achievements should be clearly indicated together with the reasons for
 shortfall, if any, in respect of the projects so that the Committee can make proper assessment of the projects executed by
 the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways.

ANALYSIS OF ANNUAL PLAN 2003-04
(Recommendation at Para 9)

5. The Committee observes that the Budget Estimates of Ministry of Shipping include allocation of
Rs.10.06 crores for execution of civil works through CPWD for DG (Shipping). The amount earmarked
is also reflected in the Demands for Grants of Ministry of Urban Development and is spent by CPWD
on the projects of the Ministry of Shipping The Committee is of the view that the practice of showing
the same amount in Demands for Grants of two Ministries creates confusion and therefore recommends
that this practice should be reviewed and the amount for the civil works should be reflected in Demands
for Grants of the Ministry of Shipping only and placed at the disposal of Ministry of Shipping instead
of Ministry of Urban Development in order to ensure better implementation, control and monitoring of
projects

REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT

6. The plan funds in respect of civil works undertaken by CPWD are reflected only in one place 1.९.
in the Demands for Grants of Ministry of Urban Development and Poverty Alleviation. However, in the
information prepared for Department-rclated Parliamentary Standing Committec, the figures of these plan
funds were reflected just to indicate the total Annual Plan allocation of DG (Shipping), The matter was,
however, taken up with Ministry of Urban Development for their views. The comments offered by them
are as under:-

~The plan provisions of not only Ministry of Shipping but also various other Ministries are also
provided in the Demands for Grants of Ministry of Urban Development for execution of civil works


2

through CPWD, As the procedure for execution of civil works is very lengthy, some times projects
carmarked by a Ministry for a particular year can not be started in that particular year due to delay in
receipt of Administrative Approval and Expenditure Sanction by CPWD, Funds earmarked for such
Projects cannot be utilized during that year and are required to be cither diverted or surrendered. The
advantage of having the funds for all the Ministries under the Demands for Grants of Ministry of Urban
Development, instead of Demands for Grants of cach concerned Ministry is that, in case, duc to some
reason the some of the projects of one Ministry are delayed, it can be utilized for another Ministry's
Projects, which may be at an advanced stage, In this way better utilization of the overall plan provisions
for civil construction of the Government as a whole is achieved.

Sometimes delay in execution of works by CPWD is caused by lack of interaction between the
Project sanctioning authority, 16, the administrative Ministry and CPWD. A system of periodic review of
the works at the level of the Scerctary (Urban Development) has been introduced to improve physical
and financial progress of various projects. Ministries have been requested to nominate a Nodal Officer
for the department, who could coordinate with CPWD to ensure timely completion of projects. CPWD
has been asked to make available to all Ministrics a monthly Progress report in respect of works being
done for various Ministrics. It is expected that the newly introduced system will go a long way in ensuring
better implementation, control, and monitoring of projects as observed by the Standing Committee of
Ministry of Shipping”

FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE

7 The Committce agrees to the view of the Ministry of Urban Development and Poverty
Alleviation that it is advantageous to have plan funds in respect of Civil works undertaken by
CPWD for all the Ministries under the Demands for Grants of Ministry of Urban Development
and Poverty Alleviation, instead of Demands for Grants of each concerned Ministries as for any
reason, if some of the projects of one Ministry are delayed then the funds can be utilized for
another Ministry's projects. Further, to improve physical and financial progress of various projects
a# system of periodic review of the works at the level of the Secretary, Urban Development and
tem of sending monthly progress report in respect of works being done for various Ministry
ave been introduced. Ministries have also been requested to nominate a nodal officer who could
coordinate with CPWD to ensure timely completion of projects. The Committee hopes that the
newly introduced system by the Ministries would ensure better implementation, control and
monitoring of projects.

DEVELOPMENT OF INTERMEDIATE AND MINOR PORTS
(Recommendation at para 23)

14 The Committee notes that the minor ports serve not only as trans-shipment points for trade but also
as catalysts for cconomic activities in their respective regions, The role of minor ports is becoming
increasingly important owing to the development of coastal shipping and they should be viewed as an
alternative to congested major ports. The Committee recommends that Ministry of Shipping should
impress upon the concerned States to provide adequate funds for the development of minor ports so that
they could effectively cater to coastal vessels and assist in development of the hinterland. The Committee
also recommends that keeping in view the contribution and importance of minor ports in cargo handling,
Government of India may also consider to provide central grants to the Maritime States for development
of Minor Ports

REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT

15. The recommendations of the Hon"ble Committee to provide adequate funds for the development of
munor ports so that they could effectively cater to coastal vessels and assist in development of the
hinterland haye been brought to the notice of all the maritime States and Union Territories with the request
to take necessary action on the recommendations.

16. The recommendations of the Hon’ble Committee for providing central grant to the maritime States
for development of minor ports was taken up with the Planning Commission. The Planning Commission


has, in response, stated that the services provided by the ports i.e. cargo handling services, berthing and
ship repair services and harbour services can be provided by the private sector more efficiently. According
to the Planning Commission, the focus of services and efficiency required in order to reform the Port
Sector could only be achicved by the private providers who are subject to competitive pressure and thus,
there is little need for additional public investment in port infrastructure. In view of this, the Planning
Commission has not agreed to the proposal to introduce a scheme relating to central grant to the maritime
States for development of minor ports. However, an amount of Rs.! crore has been allocated in the
Central Budget to the Ministry of Shipping during 2003-04 as part of Central Plan Schemes for grants
in aid to State Government for conducting feasibility/hydrographical/environmental studics for development
of minor ports.

FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE

17 The Committee is not satisfied with the reply of Ministry of Shipping for development of
minor ports in the country. The Committce recommends that the Ministry of Shipping should
keep pursuing Planning Commission for providing grants in aid to State Governments for
development of minor ports as minor ports are becoming increasingly important owing to the
development of coastal shipping and to serve as an alternative to congested major ports.

 90) of the Department of Culture, which was presented to the Parliament on 25th April 2003.

4.         On scrutiny of the said Action Taken Replies, the Committee has made observations on each item of the action
 taken/proposed to be taken by the Ministry.  The recommendations of the Committee contained in the Sixty-eight
 Report, action taken thereon by the Government and recommendations/observations of the Committee on each item of
 action taken have been given in the succeeding paragraphs.
 
THE APPROACH IN THE 10
TH PLAN AND ANALYSIS OF THE ANNUAL PLAN 2003-04 (Recommendation
 at para 10)
 
5.         The Committee observes that for the 10 th plan an amount of Rs.1720 crores inclusive of Rs.180 crores for
 Capital Component has been allocated for plan expenditure of the Department of Culture.  Out of which only Rs.250
 crores had been allocated during the first year of the 10
th Plan i.e. 2002-03 and an amount of Rs.250 crores has been
 allocated in B.E. 2003-04 as the plan outlay of Department of Culture against the projected requirement of Rs.399
 crores.  The Committee is constrained to note that the share of the Department in terms of total plan allocation of the
 Government is only 0.2 per cent, which is abysmally low.  The Committee finds that the plan outlay approved by the
 Government of India is on lower side in comparison to the amount proposed by the Department of Culture for 2003-
04.  The Committee feels that the Government has not paid adequate attention to this Sector. The Committee
 disapproves the low pace of allocation of outlay to the Department of Culture out of the total approved allocation
 outlay, i.e. of Rs.1720 crores for the plan expenditure to be made during the 10
th five-year plan.  The Committee feels
 that any reduction in the outlay would have serious implications in the development activities of the Department.  The
 Committee, recommends that in future the Department should be allocated with more funds in order to enable them to
 fulfill the targets and the Government of India should address the financial requirements of the Department of Culture
 more realistically and allocate the amount more judiciously while sanctioning the plan outlay for the remaining periods
 of the 10th Plan.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
 
6.         The matter has been taken up with the Planning Commission and their comments are awaited.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
 
7.         The Committee notes the reply and desires the Department of Culture to pursue the matter with the
 Planning Commission for allocation of more funds to Department for the remaining period of the 10
th Plan.
 
REDUCTION OF CAPITAL WORKS ALLOCATION OF THE DEPARTMENT OF CULTURE AT R.E.
 STAGE BY MINISTRY OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT
(Recommendation at para 14)
 
8.         The Committee observes that the Budget Estimates of Department of Culture also include allocation for the
 capital works.  The amount earmarked for capital works is also reflected in the Demands for Grants of Ministry of
 Urban Development.  The money is spent by CPWD on the projects of Department of Culture.  The Committee took
 serious note of the reduction of the amount at Revised Estimate stage by the Ministry of Urban development
 unilaterally that too without taking them into confidence. The Committee also notes that the capital works outlay during
 IX Plan was Rs.112 crores and CPWD could spend only Rs.59.29 crores i.e. 52.94 per cent of the total allocation,
 where as projects of Department of Culture suffered severe financial crunch.  Therefore, the Committee recommends
 that this anomalous practice should be stopped at once.  The Committee further recommends that the amount for the
 capital works should be allocated in the Demands for Grants of the Department of Culture and placed at the disposal of
 Department of Culture instead of Ministry of Urban Development in order to ensure better implementation control and
 monitoring of projects.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
